# Repository audit — 2026-09-22

## Scope and preserved material

Audited baseline: `8aa768e018315f1ee6879d7e149ea70a416c63c0` on `main`.
This review covers repository infrastructure, contribution permissions, publication, indexing and licensing. It is not an independent replication or peer review of the research claims in ORI-000001.

ORI-000001 retains its original ID, `2026-09-08T15:10:12+03:00` timestamp, folder, experiment code, manuscript, figures and data. The owner requested CC0 for original material under their control; third-party rights and dependencies are not relicensed. Existing author records remain optional provenance.

## Findings and changes

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| A PR could supply the validator and ownership files used to judge itself. | A trusted-main publisher reads immutable Git blobs through the API and checks the current main registry. It never executes submitted code. |
| The general Actions bot had a blanket maintainer exemption. | Numeric GitHub account IDs identify authors; only a narrowly scoped, fully regenerated platform PR can use the publication path. |
| Index maintenance created a fresh branch/PR per run and changed timestamps on no-op builds. | One reusable `automation/ori-platform` branch/PR; deterministic content comparison preserves timestamps on no-op and pending retries. |
| Independent allocations could propose the same next ID while earlier PRs remained unmerged. | One serialized publication workflow scans the current registry and all open eligible submissions; published IDs are unique and never reused. |
| Bot-generated PR checks could remain approval-gated; errors were hidden by `|| true`. | The trusted publisher independently validates the candidate and reports the required Checks API result; merge failures remain explicit/pending without bypassing branch rules. |
| Only shortened text and derived fields were available in the machine catalog. | All admitted Markdown documents are included with full text, Git hashes and file inventory. Oversize/truncated inputs fail visibly rather than silently disappearing. |
| Keyword inference used substring matches and incomplete stopwords. | Whole-token English matching, bilingual terms, filtered stopwords and an explicit rule-based classification label. |
| The old license required notices/attribution inconsistent with the owner's new request. | Standard CC0 1.0 legal text, a scoped dedication statement and explicit contributor consent. Citation metadata becomes optional. |
| Research reproduction instructions overstated package completeness. | Clarified which archived outputs the current script actually writes; no research result was invented or modified. |

## Tests

`python3 .github/ori/tests/test_platform.py` passes **56 automated tests locally**. Coverage includes complete synthetic Issue-to-PR-to-merge publication, simultaneous submissions, stable pending retries, recovery after branch creation, full-text coverage, no-op rebuilds, tampered ownership/control files, cross-owner edits/renames, Unicode Markdown, symlinks/submodules, deletion tombstones, licensing consent, and base/head changes before merge.

Tests use synthetic in-memory data; no fake research Idea is published and no uploaded research program is executed. Production verification is recorded separately in the audit PR and Actions logs; passing these tests does not prove the absence of all vulnerabilities.

## Remaining boundaries

- External search indexing, semantic classification correctness and scientific novelty are not guaranteed.
- GitHub event/schedule delivery is best effort. A full hourly scan and manual `Run workflow` recover missed events.
- CC0 cannot transfer rights a contributor lacks, does not grant patents/trademarks and operates only to the extent permitted by applicable law.
- Third-party copyright notices and research-integrity obligations remain relevant.
- No paid LLM service, API key, Pages website or automated research execution was enabled.
- Changes to repository About fields or administrative settings require an authorized settings interface. The existing main rules are retained.
